title: Fix it together: the search that gave up too soon
idea: GUIDED (UEPCC), bug-focused. contains() has 'return False' INSIDE the loop, so it quits on the first non-match. Move the False out so the whole list is searched.
problem: contains(nums, target) should return True if the target is anywhere in the list. But 'return False' is inside the loop, so contains([1, 2, 3], 3) wrongly returns False. Fix it.

exercises.prompt: PROBLEM: contains([1, 2, 3], 3) wrongly returns False because 'return False' is inside the loop. What SHOULD it return?
exercises.explanation: 3 is in the list, so the answer is True. The bug makes it quit before reaching the 3.

exercises.prompt: Understand — why does 'return False' inside the loop cause this?
options: It returns False on the very first item that doesn't match, never reaching the rest
exercises.explanation: On item 1 (not the target), the inner 'return False' ends the helper immediately — items 2 and 3 are never checked.
3 is right there at the end. The correct answer is True; the buggy helper never looks that far.

exercises.prompt: Returning True on a match is correct — the bug is only the EARLY 'return False'.
exercises.explanation: Yes — True-on-match is right. The mistake is returning False too soon, before the whole list is seen.

exercises.prompt: Plan the fix. Where must 'return False' go?
options: AFTER the loop — only false if nothing matched the WHOLE list
exercises.explanation: False belongs after the loop, so it's returned only when the entire list had no match.

blocks: Hand-check: 3 IS in the list, so True
See it returns False on item 1
exercises.explanation: Hand answer, spot the early False, move it out, re-check. The False must be the last line.

exercises.prompt: Code the fixed helper (return False OUTSIDE the loop).
exercises.explanation: Return True on a match inside the loop; return False only AFTER the loop ends with no match. Placement is the whole fix.

exercises.prompt: Which line must sit OUTSIDE (after) the loop?
exercises.explanation: return True stays inside (fires on a match); return False moves out, so it only runs when the whole list missed.

exercises.prompt: Check — the fixed contains([1, 2, 3], 3) returns True; hand answer was True. Verdict?
exercises.explanation: Output (True) matches the hand answer. Moving 'return False' out let the full list be searched.

exercises.prompt: Re-check: contains([1, 2, 3], 9). What does the fixed helper return?
options: False — 9 isn't there, loop ends, then return False
exercises.explanation: 9 is absent, so no match fires and the after-loop 'return False' runs. Both outcomes now work. You fixed a search bug!
